data.narrative:
Orchid is a Series A-stage biotech company within the broader Biotech & Health sector. The valuation framework draws on a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals, though narrow peer matching constraints limit direct application of median-based methods.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method here. Using the $16.5M total raised as a baseline proxy for current valuation, a 2.0x step-up multiplier—standard for Series A to subsequent-stage advancement—yields an implied valuation of $33M. The public comps in Biotech & Health trade at a median EV/Sales multiple of 7.4x, but this cannot be applied without Orchid's revenue data, which private companies typically do not disclose. Peer-median pricing is also inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within tighter valuation tiers; the broader peer set of 7 same-sector companies does not provide the minimum 3 datapoints needed for reliable narrowband triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $28M to $38M, centered at $33M. This range reflects a ±15% variance band around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue-based anchoring and limited comparable transaction data at Orchid's specific stage and market position within frontier biotech. Validation would benefit from direct revenue disclosure or higher-stage funding comparables in the cell and gene therapy space.
